cat("# BCF file (", as.character(.version), ")", sep="")

## Overview

The `bcf_file` specification describes the on-disk representation of a BCF file.
This allows more complex objects to portably store a reference to a BCF file, e.g., a [`simple_list`](../simple_list) object of multiple files.

## Object metadata

The `OBJECT` file should contain a `bcf_file` property, itself a JSON object with the following properties:

- `version`, a string specifying the version of the `bcf_file` format.
```{r, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
cat("  This should be set to \"", as.character(.version), "\".", sep="")
```

## Directory structure

### Contents

The directory should contain:

- `OBJECT`, a JSON file as described above.
- `file.bcf`, a BCF file.

Optionally, it may also contain one or both of:

- `file.bcf.tbi`, a Tabix file.
- `file.bcf.csi`, a CSI index file.

### `file.bcf`

The `file.bcf` file should be formatted as described in 
[version 1](https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/BCFv1_qref.pdf) or
[version 2](https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/BCFv2_qref.pdf)
of the BCF specification.

### `file.bcf.tbi`

The `file.bcf.tbi` file should be an index into `file.bcf`, following the [Tabix specification](https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/tabix.pdf).

### `file.bcf.csi`

The `file.bcf.csi` file should be an index into `file.bcf`, following the [CSI specification](https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/CSIv1.pdf).
